questions.question: Which of the following statements about electric charges is INCORRECT?

options.text: Electric charge is a scalar quantity.

questions.explanation: A fundamental property of electric charges is that like charges repel each other, while unlike charges attract. Statements A, B, and D are correct properties of electric charges.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about electric field lines is INCORRECT?

options.text: Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges.
Electric field lines do not form closed loops.
The tangent to an electric field line at any point gives the direction of the electric field at that point.
Two electric field lines can intersect each other.

questions.explanation: Electric field lines never intersect each other. If they did, it would mean that at the point of intersection, there would be two possible directions for the electric field, which is physically impossible.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding electric charges?

options.text: A body can have charge without having mass.
options.explanation: Charge is always associated with mass. A body cannot have charge if it has no mass, as charge resides on particles like electrons and protons which possess mass.

questions.explanation: Charge is always associated with mass. A body cannot have charge if it has no mass, as charge resides on particles like electrons and protons which possess mass. Options A, B, and C are fundamental properties of electric charge.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about electric charge is INCORRECT?

options.text: Electric charge can be destroyed by combining a proton and an electron.
Electric charge is a scalar quantity.

questions.explanation: Electric charge is always conserved; it cannot be destroyed. When a proton and an electron combine, they form a neutral hydrogen atom, but the charges themselves are still present, just balanced. Annihilation (electron-positron) converts mass to energy, but in that process, the net charge (zero) is conserved.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about electric field lines is INCORRECT?

options.text: Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges.
Electric field lines never intersect each other.
The tangent to an electric field line at any point gives the direction of the electric field at that point.
The density of electric field lines is inversely proportional to the magnitude of the electric field.

questions.explanation: The density of electric field lines (i.e., the number of lines per unit area perpendicular to the lines) is *directly* proportional to the magnitude of the electric field. Where lines are denser, the field is stronger.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding electric charge?

options.text: Electric charge is always conserved but not quantized.
options.explanation: Electric charge is both conserved and quantized.

options.text: Electric charge can be created or destroyed.
options.explanation: Electric charge is conserved and cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.

options.text: Electric charge is quantized, meaning it exists in discrete packets.
options.explanation: This statement is correct. Electric charge comes in integral multiples of the elementary charge 'e'.

options.text: The smallest unit of charge is 1 Coulomb.
options.explanation: The smallest unit of charge is the elementary charge 'e' (approximately 1.602 × 10^-19 C), not 1 Coulomb.

questions.explanation: Electric charge is quantized, meaning it exists as integral multiples of the elementary charge (e). It is also conserved. The smallest unit of charge is 'e', not 1 Coulomb.
questions.subject: icse12-physics

questions.question: Which of the following values of electric charge is NOT possible for a body?
questions.explanation: Electric charge is quantized, meaning it exists in discrete packets of elementary charge 'e' ($1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C). Any observable charge Q must be an integer multiple of 'e' (Q = ne, where n is an integer). $2.4 \times 10^{-19}$ C is not an integer multiple of $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C ($2.4/1.6 = 1.5$), hence it is not possible.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a property of electric field lines?

options.text: They originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges.
They do not form closed loops.
The tangent to an electric field line at any point gives the direction of the electric field at that point.

questions.explanation: Electric field lines never intersect each other. If they were to intersect, it would imply two different directions of the electric field at the point of intersection, which is physically impossible.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is NOT true for electric field lines?

options.text: They originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges.
The tangent to an electric field line at any point gives the direction of the electric field at that point.

questions.explanation: Electric field lines do not form closed loops. This is a property of magnetic field lines. Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges (or extend to infinity).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about electric charge is INCORRECT?

options.explanation: This statement is incorrect. Electric charge is always associated with mass.

questions.explanation: Electric charge is always associated with mass. A particle cannot have charge without having mass. For example, electrons and protons have both mass and charge. While charge itself is quantized, conserved, and scalar, its existence is intrinsically linked to matter.
